summary: Frederick M. Asher worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He spent his career at the University of Minnesota from approximately 1971 to 2021, where he served as Professor from circa 1982 until 2021.

Frederick M. Smith is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Ludo Rocher. He served as Professor at the University of Iowa (attested 2006–2008) and is attested as Professor Emeritus there in 2026.

Frederick Price was active in Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at the University of Melbourne, he served in the Madras Civil Service from 1862 to 1897 as Chief Secretary to the Government of Madras.

Frederick William Thomas specialized in Indology and Tibetology, studying at Cambridge under Edward Byles Cowell. He served as Chief Librarian at the India Office (1903–1927) and as Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford (1927–1937).

Frederick Zeuner was an archaeologist who earned his Ph.D. at Breslau after studies at Berlin and Tübingen. He held posts at the University of London, including Professor of Environmental Archaeology from 1946, and at the UCL Institute of Archaeology (~1936–1963).

Frederik David Kan Bosch studied Indology, history, and archaeology at Leiden University under Jacob Samuel Speyer, Christianus Cornelis Uhlenbeck, and Jean Philippe Vogel. He directed the Archaeological Service of the Netherlands East Indies (1916–1936) and held professorships at Utrecht and Leiden.

Fredrik Barth studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Cambridge under Edmund Leach. He held professorships at the University of Bergen (1961–1972), the University of Oslo (1974), and Boston University (~1997–2008).

Friederike Assandri works in Sinology and religious studies. She studied at Nanjing University and under Günther-Dietz Sontheimer, completing her Ph.D. at Heidelberg. She held visiting professorships at Humboldt, Leipzig, and Free University of Berlin, and researcher posts at Leipzig.

Friedhelm Hardy studied Indology and religious studies at Cologne, Heidelberg, Münster under Paul Hacker, and Oxford under Thomas Burrow and Robert Charles Zaehner. He served as Lecturer in Indian Religions at King's College London (~1975–2004).

Friedrich Adolf Krummacher was a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1785–1789). He later held a post at the University of Duisburg from approximately 1807 to 1812.

Friedrich Adolf Trendelenburg studied philosophy and linguistics at Kiel, Leipzig, and Berlin under Franz Bopp, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and August Boeckh. He served as a professor at Frederick William University Berlin from circa 1833 to 1872.

Friedrich Alexander Bischoff studied Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies at Paris under Marcelle Lalou and Robert des Rotours. He held professorships at Indiana University Bloomington (1964–1982), the University of Hamburg (1982–1993), and the University of Vienna (~1987–1998).

Friedrich August Rosen studied linguistics and Indology at Leipzig and Berlin under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer, Franz Bopp, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Henry Thomas Colebrooke. He served as Professor of Oriental Languages and Sanskrit at the University of London.

Friedrich August Wilhelm Krahmer was an Indology and religious studies scholar who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Göttingen (~1829–1833). He served as Privatdozent of Oriental Languages at the University of Marburg from 1833 to 1840.

Friedrich August Wolf, a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology, studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1777–1779). He held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1783 to 1807.

Friedrich Bechtel studied linguistics and Indology at Heidelberg, Göttingen, and Strasbourg under Theodor Benfey, August Fick, Adalbert Bezzenberger, Ernst Windisch, and Wilhelm Scherer. He lectured at Göttingen before becoming Professor of Comparative Linguistics at Halle-Wittenberg (1895–1923).

Friedrich Benedict Weber studied at the University of Leipzig (~1792–1796). He held a post at European University Viadrina (~1799–1811) and served as professor of political economy at the University of Breslau from approximately 1811 to 1848.

Friedrich Bollensen studied Indology and linguistics at Göttingen, learning Sanskrit under Heinrich Ewald. He held teaching posts in Russia, including Adjunktprofessor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1842–1858) and Professor of Sanskrit at Kazan State University (1852–1856).

Friedrich Brockhaus was an academic who held professorships at the University of Jena (~1864–1868), the University of Marburg (~1868–1871), the University of Basel (~1871–1872), and Kiel University (~1872–1895).

Friedrich Carl Andreas studied linguistics and Iranian/Central Asian studies across Halle, Erlangen, Göttingen, Leipzig, Kiel, and Copenhagen under scholars including Pott, Spiegel, and Fleischer. He taught Persian at Berlin's Seminar for Oriental Languages and became Professor at Göttingen in 1903.
